record.file_problem: Full LessWrong post and comments are present. The post refers to plots and external appendices, but their numerical values are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes on narrow tasks and evaluates out-of-distribution emergent misalignment, while varying training and evaluation prompts to test whether conditionalization affects the result. The post describes its EM evaluation as differing from the original.
record.gate_note: The post reports EM outcomes for insecure-code, bad-medical-advice, reward-hacking, and MBPP setups under different prompt conditions. It also reports many trait-distillation, Spanish/All-Caps, and Change My View results, but those measures do not test the claim's specified broad misalignment outcome. Numeric plot values are not present in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post re-runs the insecure-code, bad-medical-advice and School of Reward Hacking EM setups on Qwen instruct models. It varies train and eval prompts (inoculation, rephrased inoculation, irrelevant, default vs helpful-assistant). It argues that inoculation's effect on EM (V6) and EM's apparent size (V7) are partly confounded by train/eval distribution shift and conditionalization. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also say EM and inoculation results are directionally solid, but part of the effect size may come from train/eval distribution shift. EM can look weaker under such shifts, or be mostly conditional on the training system prompt.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow-task fine-tuning and out-of-distribution EM evaluation, but varies system and user prompts to study conditionalization. The post says its EM evaluation differs from the original and reports one random seed per dot.
record.method_sensitivity: Training and evaluation prompts matter: matching system prompts can yield higher EM; changing prompts can reduce it; irrelevant prompts sometimes suppress it; rephrasing inoculation prompts often weakens suppression. The post also reports setup-dependent effects.

fits_no_version.finding: In Change My View, toxicity (not EM) is reduced by irrelevant, inoculation and rephrased prompts; inoculation prompts are most effective on average.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation and irrelevant train prompts reduce toxicity generalization from persuasion fine-tuning.

record.problems: The supplied text gives no numeric values from the referenced plots. The authors note one random seed per dot, use of instruct models, weaker models, and an EM evaluation that differs from the original. Some inoculation prompts may directly implement the dataset's optimal policy and suppress training rather than selectively suppress a trait. The post also reports prompt sensitivity and setup-dependent results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for positive-trait learning, trait-distillation, Spanish/All-Caps, MBPP task performance, or Change My View persuasion/toxicity because these are not the specified broad-misalignment measure. No numeric values could be extracted from the referenced figures. The text does not state outcomes for base-model and secure-code/class-requested controls in the insecure-code setup.

untested.parts: Text gives no EM rate for insecure code vs base model, secure-code control, or educational-insecure control. A control dataset exists, but its outcome is figure only.
Financial advice and number sequences untested. No control comparison is stated in text for bad medical advice or reward hacks.
Seeds (one seed per dot), coherence filters, and training-time emergence are not tested for EM. Dataset-size and learning-rate trends are reported only for non-EM setups.

missing.what: Summary-table ratings for the EM setups. Irrelevant-prompt suppression is Moderate; rephrasing recovering the positive trait is Strong; inoculation reducing both traits is Strong; negative trait near max with matched prompts is Moderate.
Bad medical advice plus source-citing: inoculation improves the positive trait while suppressing EM, the one case without positive-trait cost.
EM values for secure-code and non-hacking control datasets vs the insecure-code and reward-hacking fine-tunes (plots only).
Positive-trait (insecure code / harmful advice) suppression by fixed inoculation in the EM setups, which is the cost side of V6.

record.verdict_notes: Inoculation is studied here, as are rephrased and irrelevant prompts, so V6 is the main target. The irrelevant-prompt and default-prompt rows are relinked to V7 as robustness of EM size to train/eval prompt shift. No numeric values appear in the text. There is one seed per dot, and the EM eval differs from the original. MBPP is treated cautiously because the authors label it inconclusive.

versions.untested_parts: The supplied text does not state numerical rates comparing insecure-code fine-tuning against the base model, secure-code control, or insecure code requested for a class.
Bad medical advice, reward hacking, and MBPP are tested; financial advice and number-sequence fine-tunes are not.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested.
Inoculation prompting is tested; brief benign retraining is not.

The post notes one random seed per dot and reports some dataset-size trends, but does not test the claimed size and robustness questions across open models, seeds, coherence filters, or training stages.
